prompt: A wire is bent along a circle of radius $6$ cm, forming an arc $15$ cm long. What is the central angle, in radians?
hint: You know $s = r\theta$, and this time $s$ and $r$ are given while $\theta$ is the unknown.

hints.text: You know $s = r\theta$, and this time $s$ and $r$ are given while $\theta$ is the unknown.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $r = 5$ and $s = 10$: the arc is two radius-lengths long, so $\theta = \frac{10}{5} = 2$ radians. Divide the same way here, arc on top.

explanation: Start from $s = r\theta$ and divide both sides by $r$ to get $\theta = \frac{s}{r}$.
Substitute the arc length and radius: $\theta = \frac{15}{6} = 2.5$.
The answer is $2.5$ radians — a little under $\pi$, so a bit less than a half turn, which fits an arc two and a half radius-lengths long.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count radius-lengths
steps: One radian of angle wraps exactly one radius-length of arc.
The radius is 6 cm, so ask how many 6 cm pieces fit into 15 cm.
Two and a half of them fit, so the angle is $2.5$ radians.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap answer is $0.4$, from dividing the wrong way: $\frac{6}{15}$ instead of $\frac{15}{6}$.

Check it against the picture: an arc longer than the radius must be more than one radian, so any answer under 1 is automatically wrong here. Keep the formula $\theta = \frac{s}{r}$ — arc on top, radius on the bottom.
